mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals monetary easing, reducing discount rates applied to equity cash flows and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 1250 thousand units indicate weakening consumer demand, triggering negative equity returns as construction activity and related spending expectations decline.
failure_condition: HOUST < 1250 but 20-day forward returns are positive in >60% of instances over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 100) and labor force growth (PAYEMS < 147000) signals economic contraction, causing negative equity returns through reduced corporate output and earnings expectations.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 AND PAYEMS < 147000 but 20-day returns positive in >60% of cases over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%) compress equity valuations through higher discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 2.0% but 60-day forward returns positive in >60% of instances over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Higher GDP growth (GDPC1 > 19600) signals robust economic activity, increasing corporate earnings expectations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 > 19600 but 5-day returns negative in >60% of cases over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 4.5% indicates labor market weakness, reducing consumer spending and triggering negative equity returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 4.5% but 5-day forward returns positive in >60% of instances over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 250) and low interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 1.5%) signal a 'sticky inflation' regime where real rate compression benefits equity valuations, producing positive returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 250 AND FEDFUNDS < 1.5% but 60-day returns negative in >60% of cases over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100) in late-cycle expansions signals manufacturing slowdown, causing negative equity returns as profit margins contract over 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 in late-cycle but 20-day returns positive in >60% of instances over 3-year rolling window.
